assessment.answer: The score of 0.606 comes from a balance sheet with almost no liquid assets and large losses. Current assets are 6.1% of total assets (2nd peer percentile), the current ratio is 0.17 against a peer median of 1.86, and the annualized loss is about 42.6% of assets on revenue of only $1.2M. The model probably understates the distress. The annualized net loss is reduced by non-cash fair-value gains: Q2 net loss was only $5.0M, against $110.7M in Q1. The filing itself shows $4.5M of unrestricted cash, about 0.32 months of burn, and the company survives on serial Yorkville prepaid advances that are capped and have near-term maturities. The distress is real, not an artefact.
moved_by: Unrestricted cash of $4.5M covers about 0.32 months of the $13.9M monthly six-month burn. Implied Q2 burn was about $35.9M ($83.4M six-month minus $47.5M Q1), or about $12M a month.

The only new financing is the July 2024 PPA, with about $14.1M net from the initial advance, roughly one month of burn. Further draws depend on Yorkville, the share price staying above the $1.00 floor, and the 19.99% exchange cap.

Near-term debt the cash cannot cover: $31.0M on the Tenth Pre-Paid Advance and $15.0M on the June PPA (maturing about Dec 13, 2024). Yorkville debentures were originally dated to mature Aug 30, Oct 2 and Nov 26, 2024; their remaining balances are not stated.
Cash repayment triggers and default acceleration: a VWAP below the floor or an exhausted exchange cap forces monthly cash repayments, and an event of default makes the full balance due in cash.
$58.4M of unpaid property and equipment purchases sits in current liabilities, against $33.4M of total current assets.
Funding depends on a single lender, and the advances shrink after refinancing: the $62.0M March advance netted only $15.0M after repaying prior PPAs and paying $14.0M of financing charges.
Facility reorganization and WARN notices were announced on the filing date, showing operational retrenchment.

reasons.reason: Management cannot conclude that its funding plans are probable of success. Substantial doubt has persisted since Q1 2022.
reasons.numbers: seven prior 10-Qs and two 10-Ks with substantial doubt
reasons.quote: management cannot conclude as of the date of this filing that its plans are probable of being successfully implemented.
reasons.source: 10-Q filed 2024-08-14, Note 2 - Liquidity and Capital Resources

reasons.reason: Liquidity rests entirely on the July 2024 Yorkville PPA, which is limited by the 19.99% exchange cap and the $1.00 floor.
reasons.numbers: $14.1M net initial advance; $100M aggregate limit; $1.00 floor; 19.99% cap
reasons.quote: The Company’s principal sources of liquidity are its unrestricted cash balance and the Company's principal access to capital is under the July 2024 PPA
reasons.source: 10-Q filed 2024-08-14, Note 2 - Liquidity and Capital Resources

reasons.reason: Outstanding prepaid advances can turn into cash obligations. A trigger or default makes them due in cash.
reasons.numbers: $31.0M Tenth PPA; $15.0M June PPA maturing six months after June 13, 2024; 15% default interest; 3% redemption premium
reasons.quote: the full amount outstanding under the Pre-Paid Advances plus the Redemption Premium, together with interest and other amounts owed in respect thereof, will become, at Yorkville’s election, immediately due and payable in cash.

reasons.reason: Large unpaid capex payables in current liabilities exceed all current assets.
reasons.numbers: $58,411K PP&E acquisitions in current liabilities vs $33.4M current assets
reasons.quote: Acquisition of property and equipment included in current liabilities $ 58,411 $ 68,050
reasons.source: 10-Q filed 2024-08-14, Cash flow statement - supplemental non-cash disclosures

reasons.reason: Total assets are mostly illiquid, so the 0.64 liabilities/assets ratio, close to the 0.59 peer median, overstates the cushion.
reasons.numbers: total assets $543.3M; PP&E $380.1M; deferred warrant asset $50.2M

reasons.reason: Debentures with near-term maturity dates add potential cash claims. Their remaining balances are unclear.
reasons.quote: The Initial Debenture will mature on November 26, 2024, and may be extended at Yorkville’s option.

reasons.reason: Litigation exposure adds possible cash claims.
reasons.numbers: Champ Key damages in excess of $23.0M; securities class action; employment class action filed July 8, 2024
reasons.quote: seeks injunctive relief, compensatory damages in excess of $23.0 million and punitive damages, interests, costs of suit and attorneys’ fees.

evidence_against.point: New financing closed after quarter end, and Yorkville has repeatedly refinanced and waived terms rather than enforcing them.
evidence_against.quote: net proceeds of the Initial July Prepaid Advance to the Company were approximately $14.1 million.

evidence_against.point: The aggregate July PPA limit of $100M over 24 months gives headroom if the share price and cap allow.
evidence_against.quote: with an aggregate limitation on the Prepaid Advances of $100,000,000 over the course of 24 months from the Effective Date

evidence_against.point: CEO-affiliated entities have repeatedly injected capital: Series C preferred, the 2023 common stock purchase, and the factory sale-leaseback.
evidence_against.quote: for a total aggregate purchase price of $10,000,000

evidence_against.point: The company has survived substantial doubt for more than two years, settling much of its debt in shares rather than cash.
evidence_against.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the September Convertible Debentures was fully paid off through the issuance of 3.5 million shares of Common Stock to Yorkville

evidence_against.point: Cash burn and capex are falling year over year, and first vehicles are being delivered.
evidence_against.quote: We have commercialized our first production vehicles and are delivering them to customers.

evidence_against.point: There is a possible $61.1M Section 16(b) recovery from DDG, but it is uncertain and slow.
evidence_against.quote: In the action, the Company seeks to recover an estimated $61.1 million of Section 16(b) profits.

evidence_against.point: Restricted cash of about $14.6M exists in addition to unrestricted cash, though it is not freely available.

timeline.event: Nasdaq notice of failure to meet the $1.00 minimum bid price
CEO-affiliated entity takes over the $34.2M Oklahoma City factory purchase and leases it back
Exchange Cap for Yorkville issuances nearly exhausted (~907 shares left)
$45M Series B preferred and warrants sold to an institutional investor
Seventh supplemental Yorkville advance at $0.1805; warrants exchanged for about 238M shares
$62.0M Tenth Pre-Paid Advance, mostly refinancing, with $15.0M net
10-K: substantial doubt; cash not sufficient for the next 12 months
June $15M Pre-Paid Advance (~$14.1M net), maturing in six months
July 2024 PPA: $15M initial advance (~$14.1M net), up to $100M over 24 months, $1.00 floor
Q2 10-Q: cash $4.5M, substantial doubt; Torrance reorganization and WARN notices announced

dates_to_watch: 2024-08-30: maturity date of the $26.6M Yorkville debenture (remaining balance unknown)
2024-10-02: maturity date of the $27.9M Yorkville debenture (remaining balance unknown)
2024-10-15: first separations under the Torrance reorganization
Mid-November 2024: Q3 10-Q, covering cash level, new draws and the going-concern language
About 2024-12-13: maturity of the $15.0M June Prepaid Advance
Any stockholder vote to lift the 19.99% exchange cap
Share price relative to the $1.00 PPA floor and the Nasdaq $1.00 minimum bid
would_change_my_mind: A sizeable non-Yorkville financing, such as a strategic investor, government loan or large equity raise, covering at least six months of burn
A large confirmed vehicle order with cash deposits, or meaningful revenue growth
Yorkville extending maturities and continuing draws under the $100M limit without cash repayment triggers

Toward higher risk: a missed payment or event of default, a trading halt or Nasdaq delisting notice, failure to obtain stockholder approval for the exchange cap, or the share price falling below the $1.00 floor
could_not_check: Remaining principal on the 2023 Yorkville convertible debentures maturing August to November 2024
Share price at filing date relative to the PPA trigger and floor prices
How much of the July $14.1M had been spent by the filing date, and the actual cash on 2024-08-14
Whether vendors holding the $58.4M of capex payables are pressing for payment
How much each model input contributed to the 0.606 score
